summary: aegis is an offline-first web app that lets a deep-space crew monitor its own health and act on a medical problem without waiting for Earth, where a single message can take up to 20 minutes each way. It brings together vital signs, sleep, radiation dose and mood for each crew member, who is recognized by the camera on the device. A green, yellow or red traffic light compares every reading with that person’s own baseline. When a signal goes out of range, aegis asks “Do you need help?”; if nobody answers within 30 seconds, it sounds a ship alarm and opens one of 11 step-by-step protocols with a first-aid manual based on AHA, WHO and Red Cross guidance, with no invented doses. Everything runs in airplane mode, the medical log is encrypted with a PIN, and reports are queued and sent to Earth when a link is available. It matters because on the way to Mars the caregiver is another crew member, often not a doctor, and aegis puts the guidance on board.
details:
What it does. aegis is a clinical decision-support and health-monitoring tool for crews on Moon, Mars and deep-space missions that cannot rely on real-time help from Earth (up to 20 min one-way delay, per NASA HRP). It measures, detects, guides and records:

  • Measure: vital signs (heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, temperature), sleep, radiation dose, exercise and a “How I feel” self-check with a reaction test. Inputs are modeled on real onboard devices such as Bio-Monitor, an actigraph and dosimeters. The camera recognizes each crew member on the device (MediaPipe Face Landmarker) and opens their profile.
  • Detect: an explainable rule engine compares each reading with the person’s own baseline and shows a green, yellow or red traffic light that names the signals behind each alert.
  • Respond: a full-screen “Do you need help?” prompt with a 30-second countdown. If there is no answer, or the person asks for help, a ship alarm sounds on the crew screens. 11 step-by-step protocols (unresponsive crewmate, chest pain, low oxygen, injury, dizziness, emotional crisis, solar event and more) remember the current step, and each step links to a first-aid manual.
  • Record: every event goes into an encrypted onboard log and an outbox that delivers per-crew reports to Earth when there is a link, with simulated Moon or Mars delay. Photos, video, face templates and PINs are never sent.

Benefits and impact. It works 100% offline from the first second, it is designed for non-physicians, it is bilingual (English/Spanish) and it reaches emergency protocols in fewer than three taps. It does not invent doses or thresholds: medical content comes from NASA HRP, NASA-STD-3001, CSA, AHA/ERC 2025, WHO and Red Cross.

Tools. React 19, TypeScript, Vite, PWA (vite-plugin-pwa), IndexedDB (Dexie) with AES-GCM encryption via Web Crypto, Zod, react-i18next, MediaPipe (on-device WASM), Recharts, Lucide icons. Quality: 95 unit tests (Vitest) and 22 end-to-end tests (Playwright) that run with the network blocked, plus accessibility checks with axe.

Creativity and considerations. Each person is compared with their own baseline rather than an average. Escalation to a crewmate is automatic if nobody responds. Privacy is designed in (local face matching, never stored as images). The interface is high-contrast and works under stress. Crew members and data in the demo are fictional.
